plain: This story is about an idea called the Orion correlation theory, about the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, tells it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He says it was put forward in 1994 by an author named Robert Bauval in his book The Orion Mystery. The idea is that the pyramids are laid out to match the stars of Orion's belt, three bright stars in a row in the constellation Orion. A pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm brings it up on a later episode. He describes it as showing that some of these buildings are connected to Orion's belt, and says he thinks it is true, though he does not name Bauval or the year. If true, it would mean the builders planned their monuments around the stars.
